soundness_flags.label: ass:multinomial-sampling
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Weissman condition supports iid empirical-distribution concentration, not the additional causal consistency link p_g0=μ_g^0 and p_g1=ν_g; split out a standard consistency/SUTVA assumption with an appropriate causal citation.

soundness_flags.label: ass:marginal-fit
soundness_flags.one_line: Given k_gx is defined as Pr{X(1)=z|X(0)=x,G=g}, marginal reproduction is the law of total probability, so it is an observed-data constraint defining the candidate kernel class rather than an independent causal assumption.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:tv-drift and all fixed-d endpoint/sign claims
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The upper rowwise-TV radius is not identified or empirically calibrated by randomized-arm marginals and must be supplied as a scientific sensitivity choice.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Sharp endpoints, compatibility, and sign radii are conditional on the maintained rowwise-TV shared-kernel class at each prespecified d; ρ* is only its observable feasibility lower bound.

source_verification_receipts.locator: article metadata and Summary; Sections 3 and 7 listed in article contents
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published article studies multiple-trial principal causal effects, uses cross-trial homogeneity for identification, requires at least three trials for the stated local-identification condition without monotonicity, and includes sensitivity analysis without homogeneity.
The paper assumes zero correlation between site-specific principal-stratum shares and impacts, plus nonzero variance and mean normalizations, to identify its two principal causal effects.
The paper treats binary or continuous intermediates, develops parametric continuous-intermediate outcome/principal-stratum models, and studies same-sign and dominant-observed-effect restrictions.
The paper gives a tractable sharp-identification characterization for convex moment-prediction models through Aumann-expectation geometry and convex-programming membership checks.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economic Studies 78(4), 2011 paper text
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper characterizes compatibility through capacity/core conditions, finite inequalities in regular finite-game settings, and computational checks.
The paper transforms a bounded regular linear-fractional program into a linear program by y=tx and denominator normalization.
The paper defines surrogate-paradox resilience measures under controlled deviations of Study-B functions from Study-A functions rather than a shared latent transition-kernel TV class.
The paper derives sharp nonparametric principal-effect bounds using a bounding factor based on unmeasured-confounder relative risks.
The paper proposes bootstrap calibrated projection intervals for functions of partially identified parameters in moment-(in)equality models, with a global optimization approximation algorithm.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corroborating the 2024 JBES article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The method bootstraps value functions of randomly perturbed linear programs for uniformly valid inference on linear functionals under linear moment inequalities.
The report derives L1-deviation bounds for empirical distributions of iid samples; it contains no potential-outcome consistency or treatment-to-potential-outcome observation condition.
The paper develops computable convex-underestimating programs for factorable nonconvex optimization; it does not establish the proposed exact finite profiling algorithm.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Split ass:multinomial-sampling into iid multinomial sampling and a separately cited SUTVA/consistency condition, and move marginal reproduction from assumptions into the kernel-class definition as an observed-marginal constraint.

Replace the one-off strict-improvement witness with a generic, observable sufficient condition under which d=0 pooling strictly contracts a named separate-trial PSACE interval; retain W* as a worked example.
Provide a prespecified expert-elicitation protocol or external validation design that maps trial commensurability information to defensible d-ranges, then demonstrate the full d-path on ACCT data.

recommended_next_step: Revise the causal observation assumptions and remove the redundant marginal-fit assumption; then advance the conditionally sharp shared-kernel PartialID core to Stage 0.
